label: step right after an early g input (t=2..5)
explanation: Sparse feature (0.06% of steps). About 70% of activations and activation mass fall on the step immediately after a g input, mostly at t=2..5. That includes the <DEL> step when g is the last original token (short L=3-5 sequences), and the following input when g sits mid-sequence. It never fires at t=0-1 and rarely fires late in the copy phase. The strongest activations come in sequences that start with d (first_tok d, 9.5x lift) where g is preceded by 0, y or g. A secondary weaker mode is the first copy step (outputting d) right after <DEL> in d-initial sequences. Precision is very low (about 4%): most post-g steps do not activate, so the feature depends on an extra conjunction over the prefix (d-initial, the token before g) that I could not capture as a simple predicate. The best conjunctive refinement (prev2 in {0,y,g}, t<=6) reached only F1 0.20.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=d (+4.75), prev_tok=g (+4.60), phase=2 & in_tok=v (+4.50), phase=2 & in_tok=c (+4.38), orig0=d (+3.98), t=3 & prev_tok=g (+3.70). Lower it: phase=2 (-4.20), prev2_tok=d (-3.46), prev2_tok=f (-3.34), prev2_tok=c (-3.18).
